nodes.claim: From the assumed order of $-a$, the proof obtains $a^{(p-1)/2}\equiv-1\pmod p$, hence this power is not congruent to $1$ modulo $p$.
nodes.text: Since $-a$ has order $(p-1)/2=2t+1$ modulo $p$, we have $(-a)^{2t+1}\equiv1\pmod p$. As $2t+1$ is odd, $a^{(p-1)/2}=a^{2t+1}=-(-a)^{2t+1}\equiv-1\pmod p$, so $a^{(p-1)/2}\not\equiv1\pmod p$.

reason: Replace the erroneous modulus $2$ by $p$; the order assumption gives $(-a)^{(p-1)/2}\equiv1\pmod p$, and $(p-1)/2=2t+1$ is odd.
